title: One group of weights onto sixteen levels
why: It shows the mapping the prose describes in sequence: a contiguous run of 128 entries gets one min and one max, a scale of (max-min)/15, and a zero point, so each weight lands on an integer from 0 to 15 and decodes as (q - z) times s.
nodes: contiguous 128 entries = 128 input features of one output channel
notes: Grid axes: rows are output features d_out, columns are input features d_in. Highlight one row and a contiguous run of 128 entries along it. Beside it, show a number line from min to max mapped onto integer levels 0 through 15, labelled with s and z. All quantities come from the chapter: d_out, d_in, 128, 0..15, s, z. | Left: W as a d_out-by-d_in grid, with a highlighted 128-entry contiguous run along the input dimension in one row. Middle: byte strip showing 3 metadata bytes beside 64 payload bytes, with two 4-bit codes per byte and low nibble first. Right: kernel stages from 32-bit load through shifts/masks, zero-point subtraction, scale multiply, fp16 conversion, to tensor-core multiply. Bottom: comparison across group sizes 64, 128, 256 with payload bytes, metadata bytes, overhead percentages, bits per weight where given, and outlier reach; all quantities are those stated in the section. | Flow runs left to right: X feeds H; w and H⁻¹ feed the column loop. H is estimated once per layer from 128 C4 sequences of 2048 tokens, with damping on the diagonal. Labels: d_in input dimension, n calibration examples, indices k and j. The loop holds ŵ_j at its rounded value while adjusting only columns not yet quantized; no axes, arrows show X→H and w,H⁻¹→column loop. | No axes; left-to-right dataflow. Quantities labelled where they appear in the chapter: d_in columns, block size 128, about 1% higher-precision channels, per-channel scale s_j. The worked example's error 0.2 and objective 0.16→0.12 can be shown as a small inset on the column-update stage, but the main figure carries the pipeline structure. | No axes; this is a memory layout. The super-block contains 8 sub-blocks; each sub-block has its own 6-bit scale s_k and 6-bit minimum m_k. Dequantization is w = d·s_k·q − m·m_k, where q is the 4-bit code for the weight and s_k, m_k belong to its 32-weight sub-block. Byte counts: d and m are 2 bytes each (4 bytes total); the 16 six-bit sub-block values pack into 12 bytes; the 256 four-bit codes are 128 bytes; total 144 bytes, giving 4.5 bits per weight. | Horizontal axis: feature dimension index. Vertical axis: activation magnitude, with one outlier bar at 1000 and a cluster near 1. Overlay the symmetric 8-bit grid with spacing ≈7.8, showing the cluster collapsing onto 0 or 7.8. Annotate the scale as set by the 1000 maximum and the output-error example as 0.01 × 1000 = 10; all quantities come from the chapter. | Two side-by-side panels. Left panel: prefill stage, labelled with 130,659 prompt tokens and mean 3.33 s; arrow from prompt tokens into a batched matmul block. Right panel: decode stage, labelled with 607 tokens and mean 8.38 s; sequence of single-token steps, with the limiting quantity 4.19 bits per weight pulled from memory. No invented numbers; all labelled quantities come from the section.
note: Per group of 128 input features: s = (max - min)/15, z = round(-min/s), q = clamp(round(w/s)+z, 0, 15), and the decode is (q - z) * s.
